def init_mapping(self):
    import math
    from collections import defaultdict

    N = self.num_qubits
    self.mapping_dict = [None] * N
    self.reverse_mapping_dict = [None] * N

    # ---- Step 1: collect 2q interactions in temporal order ----
    try:
        sorted_gate_ids = sorted(self.access.keys())
    except Exception:
        sorted_gate_ids = list(self.access.keys())

    interactions = []
    depth_idx = 0
    logical_qubits = set()
    for gid in sorted_gate_ids:
        qubits = self.access[gid]
        if qubits is None:
            continue
        for q in qubits:
            if isinstance(q, int) and 0 <= q < N:
                logical_qubits.add(q)
        if len(qubits) == 2:
            q1, q2 = qubits[0], qubits[1]
            if q1 == q2:
                continue
            if not (0 <= q1 < N and 0 <= q2 < N):
                continue
            interactions.append((q1, q2, depth_idx))
            depth_idx += 1

    M = len(interactions)
    alpha = 3.0 / max(M, 1)

    # ---- Step 2: temporally decayed weighted interaction graph ----
    interaction_weight = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))
    for q1, q2, d in interactions:
        w = math.exp(-alpha * d)
        interaction_weight[q1][q2] += w
        interaction_weight[q2][q1] += w

    total_weight = {q: sum(interaction_weight[q].values()) for q in logical_qubits}

    # ---- Step 3: physical centrality (lower distance-sum => more central) ----
    centrality_cache = [
        sum(self.distance_matrix[p][q] for q in range(N)) for p in range(N)
    ]
    max_centrality = max(centrality_cache) if centrality_cache else 1.0
    centrality_norm = max_centrality if max_centrality > 0 else 1.0

    # ---- Step 4: hardware adjacency (for attachment-boundary growth) ----
    phys_neighbors = [set() for _ in range(N)]
    try:
        for p in range(N):
            adj = self.backend[p] if p < len(self.backend) else []
            for q in adj:
                if 0 <= q < N and q != p:
                    phys_neighbors[p].add(q)
    except Exception:
        try:
            for (a, b) in self.backend_connections:
                if 0 <= a < N and 0 <= b < N and a != b:
                    phys_neighbors[a].add(b)
                    phys_neighbors[b].add(a)
        except Exception:
            pass

    used_physical = [False] * N
    placed_logical = set()
    boundary = set()  # h5: physical qubits adjacent to any placed slot

    LOOKAHEAD_DECAY = 0.35
    CENTRALITY_TIE = 1e-3

    # ---- Step 5: single-vertex seed (heaviest weighted degree -> most central phys) ----
    if logical_qubits:
        seed_logical = max(
            logical_qubits,
            key=lambda q: (total_weight.get(q, 0.0), -q),
        )
        best_phys = None
        best_score = None
        for p in range(N):
            s = centrality_cache[p]
            if best_score is None or s < best_score or (s == best_score and p < best_phys):
                best_score = s
                best_phys = p
        self.mapping_dict[seed_logical] = best_phys
        self.reverse_mapping_dict[best_phys] = seed_logical
        used_physical[best_phys] = True
        placed_logical.add(seed_logical)
        for nb in phys_neighbors[best_phys]:
            if not used_physical[nb]:
                boundary.add(nb)

    remaining = set(logical_qubits) - placed_logical

    # ---- Step 6: ITERATIVE ATTACHMENT GROWTH (hypothesis h5) ----
    # Restrict next-placement candidates to the current attachment boundary
    # (physical neighbors of already-placed slots). The boundary is NOT a
    # precomputed/fixed frontier — it grows dynamically as new qubits are
    # placed, so previously-pruned physical qubits become reachable later
    # once interaction weights accumulate. This preserves a contiguous
    # embedding boundary at every step.
    while remaining:
        # Pick the logical qubit with the strongest accumulated tie to placed set
        best_cand = None
        best_cand_weight = -1.0
        best_cand_total = -1.0
        for q in remaining:
            w = 0.0
            nbrs = interaction_weight.get(q, {})
            for nbr, wt in nbrs.items():
                if nbr in placed_logical:
                    w += wt
            tw = total_weight.get(q, 0.0)
            if (w > best_cand_weight) \
               or (w == best_cand_weight and tw > best_cand_total) \
               or (w == best_cand_weight and tw == best_cand_total
                   and (best_cand is None or q < best_cand)):
                best_cand_weight = w
                best_cand_total = tw
                best_cand = q

        if best_cand is None:
            break

        placed_neighbors = [
            (nbr, wt) for nbr, wt in interaction_weight.get(best_cand, {}).items()
            if nbr in placed_logical
        ]
        unplaced_neighbors = [
            (nbr, wt) for nbr, wt in interaction_weight.get(best_cand, {}).items()
            if nbr not in placed_logical and nbr != best_cand
        ]

        # h5: candidate slots are exactly the live attachment boundary.
        # Fall back to any unused phys qubit only if the boundary is empty
        # (disconnected coupling graph, or no seed had any neighbors).
        candidate_phys = [p for p in boundary if not used_physical[p]]
        if not candidate_phys:
            candidate_phys = [p for p in range(N) if not used_physical[p]]

        best_phys = None
        best_cost = None
        for p in candidate_phys:
            if placed_neighbors:
                d = 0.0
                for nbr, wt in placed_neighbors:
                    d += wt * self.distance_matrix[p][self.mapping_dict[nbr]]
                if unplaced_neighbors:
                    avg_dist_to_placed = 0.0
                    cnt = 0
                    for pl in placed_logical:
                        avg_dist_to_placed += self.distance_matrix[p][self.mapping_dict[pl]]
                        cnt += 1
                    if cnt > 0:
                        avg_dist_to_placed /= cnt
                    d += LOOKAHEAD_DECAY * sum(wt for _, wt in unplaced_neighbors) * avg_dist_to_placed
                cost = d + CENTRALITY_TIE * (centrality_cache[p] / centrality_norm)
            else:
                cost = centrality_cache[p]
            if best_cost is None or cost < best_cost or (cost == best_cost and p < best_phys):
                best_cost = cost
                best_phys = p

        if best_phys is None:
            break

        self.mapping_dict[best_cand] = best_phys
        self.reverse_mapping_dict[best_phys] = best_cand
        used_physical[best_phys] = True
        placed_logical.add(best_cand)
        remaining.discard(best_cand)

        # h5: dynamically expand the attachment boundary
        boundary.discard(best_phys)
        for nb in phys_neighbors[best_phys]:
            if not used_physical[nb]:
                boundary.add(nb)

    # ---- Step 7: identity-preferred fallback for any unmapped logical qubits ----
    for l in range(N):
        if self.mapping_dict[l] is None:
            if l < N and not used_physical[l]:
                self.mapping_dict[l] = l
                self.reverse_mapping_dict[l] = l
                used_physical[l] = True
            else:
                for p in range(N):
                    if not used_physical[p]:
                        self.mapping_dict[l] = p
                        self.reverse_mapping_dict[p] = l
                        used_physical[p] = True
                        break

    assert len(set(self.mapping_dict)) == len(self.mapping_dict)

h0.statement: Weighting recent two-qubit interactions more heavily than older ones via temporal_decay_weighting reduces SWAPs because the initial mapping aligns physical adjacency with the gates executed earliest, where misplacements compound into long routing chains before any natural rebalancing can occur.

h1.statement: Seeding placement from a centrally located physical qubit (central_physical_seed) lowers SWAP counts because subsequent neighbor expansions inherit shorter average shortest-path distances to all other physical qubits than expansions seeded from peripheral nodes, bounding worst-case routing distance for later-placed logical qubits.

h2.statement: Anchoring the highest-degree logical qubit first (highest_degree_logical_seed) at the central physical seed reduces SWAPs because the qubit with the most interaction partners is placed where it can satisfy the largest number of adjacency constraints simultaneously, minimizing the count of edges that must later be bridged by routing.

h3.statement: Greedy assignment that minimizes a sum of interaction-weighted distances (weighted_distance_cost_minimization) restricted to the physical_neighbor_candidate_filter outperforms unrestricted placement because constraining candidates to neighbors of already-placed qubits enforces a connected, locality-preserving frontier, preventing the placement of strongly-interacting logical qubits onto disconnected hardware regions that would later require long SWAP chains.

h4.statement: Edge_pair_seed_placement increases SWAP counts relative to single-vertex centrality seeding because committing two physical qubits to one logical edge at initialization over-constrains the placement frontier, forcing subsequent high-degree logical qubits onto suboptimal physical positions whose cumulative routing cost exceeds the savings of pre-satisfying one edge.

h5.statement: Iterative_attachment_growth reduces SWAP counts compared to frontier_restricted_candidates because growing the placement one qubit at a time from already-placed neighbors preserves a contiguous embedding boundary, whereas restricting candidates to a fixed frontier set prematurely prunes physical qubits that would later become optimal attachment points once interaction weights accumulate.

h6.statement: Weighted_distance_cost_minimization outperforms reciprocal_distance_centrality scoring because summing interaction-weighted shortest-path distances directly approximates the routing cost objective, while reciprocal-distance centrality conflates topological prominence with interaction relevance and rewards physical hubs even when no high-interaction logical qubit needs them.

h7.statement: Combining highest_degree_logical_seed with iterative_attachment_growth lowers SWAPs because anchoring the densest logical hub first establishes a high-constraint nucleus, and incremental neighbor attachment then resolves the remaining qubits in decreasing order of constraint pressure, preventing late-stage placements from being forced into disconnected regions.

h8.statement: Centrality_tiebreak among equally-scoring placement candidates reduces SWAPs because when multiple physical qubits yield identical weighted-distance costs, selecting the more central one preserves shorter expected paths for not-yet-placed logical qubits, whereas arbitrary tiebreaking can strand future placements at the periphery.

h9.statement: Frontier_restricted_candidates inflates SWAP counts relative to iterative_attachment_growth because hard-restricting candidates to the current frontier ignores globally cheaper placements that lie one hop beyond the frontier, producing locally optimal but globally suboptimal embeddings whose later qubits incur disproportionate routing penalties.

archive.name: spectral_laplacian_coembedding
archive.description: Embed both the logical interaction graph and the physical coupling graph using low-order eigenvectors of their (weighted) Laplacians, then align the two point sets by sorting along the Fiedler direction and pairing in rank order. Captures global graph geometry in a closed-form way rather than greedy local decisions.

archive.name: landmark_distance_fingerprint_matching
archive.description: Pick a small set of landmark physical qubits, compute each physical qubit's distance-vector signature to them, then build analogous interaction-weighted signatures for logical qubits, and match by nearest signature. Treats placement as a metric-embedding problem with O(L) dimensions.

archive.name: edge_priority_kruskal_placement
archive.description: Process logical interactions edge-first in descending weight order and lay each edge onto a physical edge, rather than growing a tree or ordering nodes. This directly materializes the heaviest interactions as physical adjacencies, and unlike MST-based methods considers cycles and parallel heavy edges.

archive.name: weighted_edge_priority_anchored_growth_c0_1
archive.description: Greedy placement that processes logical edges in descending interaction-weight order, seeds the heaviest pair on the highest-combined-degree physical edge, and grows the cluster by placing each new logical qubit on the free physical neighbor that minimizes weighted shortest-path distance to its already-mapped logical neighbors (with degree as tiebreaker, falling back to global distance_matrix lookups when no adjacent slot is free).

archive.name: central_seed_heavy_edge_growth_c0_2
archive.description: Sorts the logical interaction graph by edge weight and seeds the heaviest edge onto the most central physical qubit (low eccentricity, high degree) plus its highest-degree neighbor; subsequent unmapped endpoints are placed at the free physical qubit minimizing the weighted-distance sum to *all* already-placed logical neighbors, breaking ties by physical degree.

archive.name: temporal_decay_landmark_anchored_greedy_c0_4
archive.description: Builds a temporally-decayed weighted interaction graph and seeds the top weighted-degree logical qubits onto a farthest-first set of central physical landmarks (matched by physical centrality), then iteratively places remaining qubits greedily by minimizing total weighted distance to already-placed neighbors with centrality-based tie-breaking, and falls back to identity for unused qubits.

archive.name: temporal_dyad_seeded_weighted_growth_c0_0
archive.description: Builds a temporally-decayed weighted interaction graph over logical qubits, seeds the heaviest weighted edge on an adjacent pair of maximum-centrality physical qubits (dyad seeding), then iteratively places remaining logicals in order of connection strength to the placed set, choosing the free physical qubit that minimizes the weighted sum of distances to already-placed partners with a small centrality tiebreak.

archive.name: greedy_weighted_frontier_with_lookahead_placement_c0_5
archive.description: Anchors the highest weighted-degree logical qubit at the physical qubit with minimum total-distance centrality, then greedily expands the placed frontier by selecting the unplaced logical qubit with the largest connection weight to already-placed qubits and mapping it to the unused physical qubit minimizing a weighted distance cost that combines placed-neighbor proximity with a discounted look-ahead term over unplaced neighbors and a small physical-centrality tie-breaker.

archive.name: central_seed_adjacency_biased_weighted_growth_c0_9
archive.description: Seeds the highest-weight logical qubit at the physical graph centroid (minimum sum-of-distances node, tiebroken by highest degree), then iteratively places the remaining logical qubit with the largest cumulative interaction weight to already-placed qubits at the free physical slot minimizing weighted distance to its mapped neighbors, using direct physical adjacency count and node degree as tiebreakers to bias toward high-connectivity hubs.

archive.name: recursive_graph_bisection_alignment
archive.description: Recursively bisect both the weighted interaction graph and the coupling graph and assign matched halves to each other. This is a top-down METIS-style placement that preserves cut structure: heavy intra-half edges land in connected physical regions, while light inter-half edges absorb the only physical "cut" they cross. It optimizes global cut locality before any local greedy decision.

archive.name: maximum_weight_matching_pair_placement
archive.description: Treat the heaviest interactions as a set of disjoint pairs via a maximum-weight matching on the interaction graph, then drop those pairs onto adjacent coupling edges. Singletons and lighter edges fill in afterwards by greedy adjacency. The primitive is matching (not growth), which guarantees the top heavy interactions become adjacent simultaneously rather than sequentially-conflicting.

archive.name: attraction_weighted_growth_placement
archive.description: Grow the mapping one qubit at a time, where the next logical qubit chosen is the one with maximum aggregate interaction weight to the already-placed set, and its physical slot minimizes the sum of weighted distances to its already-placed logical neighbors. Differs from tree/MST embeddings because it uses the full weighted graph and multi-parent distance sums, not a predetermined tree.

archive.name: centrality_anchored_temporal_growth_c0_3
archive.description: Builds a temporally-decayed weighted interaction graph (early gates matter most), seeds the highest-weighted-degree logical qubit onto the most central physical qubit (closeness via `Σ 1/d`), then iteratively grows the mapping by picking the logical qubit with the strongest ties to the already-placed set and placing it on the unused physical that minimizes weighted distance to placed neighbors, with a mild centrality lookahead term so qubits still expecting future interactions avoid peripheral sites.

archive.name: personalized_pagerank_signature_matching
archive.description: Compute a Personalized PageRank vector for every qubit on its own graph, producing a topology fingerprint that captures multi-hop neighborhood mass. Match logical and physical qubits by sorting these signatures and pairing rank-by-rank, so qubits that "see" their graph in similar ways are aligned. Unlike landmark shortest-path methods, PPR is smooth and weight-aware.

archive.name: eccentricity_peripheral_central_split
archive.description: Sort logical qubits by total weighted interaction (centrality of activity) and physical qubits by inverse eccentricity (how close they are to all others). Then place high-activity logical at low-eccentricity physical and low-activity logical at high-eccentricity physical. This is a one-pass rank–rank assignment that exploits the peripheral/central asymmetry of real coupling graphs.

archive.name: densest_weighted_subgraph_core_embedding
archive.description: Extract the densest weighted subgraph of the interaction graph (the cluster of qubits with maximum average internal weight) and embed it into the densest connected subgraph of the coupling graph. The remaining logical qubits are appended by weighted-attraction BFS expansion. This focuses placement effort where it matters: the heavy interaction core.

archive.name: articulation_bridge_aware_placement
archive.description: Identify articulation points and bridges in the coupling graph and treat them as scarce routing resources. Place high-betweenness logical qubits on articulation physical qubits and avoid forcing heavy interactions across bridges. The mapping is built by partitioning logical qubits according to which physical biconnected component they should live in.

archive.name: clustering_coefficient_locality_alignment
archive.description: Match logical qubits to physical qubits by similarity of weighted local clustering coefficient — a measure of how much each qubit's neighbors interact with each other. Triangle-rich logical qubits land on triangle-rich physical positions, preserving local 3-cycle structure that makes routing within a neighborhood cheap.

archive.name: temporal_stratified_priority_placement
archive.description: Unlike purely topological approaches, weight interactions by when they occur in the circuit — early-layer 2-qubit gates matter more because an initial mapping primarily amortizes over the opening layers before SWAPs reshape things. Build the placement around an interaction graph whose weights decay with gate depth.

archive.name: centrality_seeded_weighted_attraction_placement_c0_7
archive.description: Seeds the most-interactive logical qubit onto the physical qubit with minimum total shortest-path distance (graph centroid), then iteratively places the remaining logicals in order of greatest weighted attraction to the already-placed set, choosing each physical slot that minimizes the weighted sum of distances to mapped neighbors, with physical-degree used as a tie-breaker to favor hub slots.

archive.name: single_vertex_centrality_seeded_temporal_decay_greedy_c0_0
archive.description: Builds a temporally-decayed weighted interaction graph over logical qubits, then deliberately seeds with a single highest-weighted-degree logical qubit placed on the most centrally-located physical qubit (rejecting edge-pair seeding per the hypothesis to avoid over-constraining the frontier), and grows the mapping by iteratively selecting the unplaced logical qubit with the strongest connection to the placed set and assigning it to the unused physical qubit minimizing the weighted sum of distances to already-placed neighbors.

archive.name: temporal_decay_weighted_greedy_with_early_window_boost_c0_1
archive.description: Builds a logical interaction graph in which earlier two-qubit gates carry exponentially larger weight (stronger temporal decay than the parents, plus an explicit early-window multiplier on the first gates), then seeds the heaviest logical on the most central physical qubit and grows the embedding by greedy attachment that prefers free physical neighbors of already-placed qubits, breaking ties by physical centrality and weighted distance cost.

archive.name: single_vertex_centroid_anchored_weighted_growth_c0_5
archive.description: Anchors the placement with one single highest-interaction-weight logical qubit pinned to the topologically most central physical qubit (explicitly avoiding any two-vertex/edge-pair seed commitment), then grows the mapping greedily by selecting the unplaced logical qubit with maximum weighted attachment to the placed set and locating it at the unused physical qubit minimizing weighted distance to placed neighbors with adjacency-bonus, physical-degree, and a small lookahead-decay term over yet-unplaced interactions as tiebreakers.
